text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

CORN SALE - The U.S. Agriculture Department Wednesday said private exporters reported sales of 500,000 tonnes of corn to Egypt. USDA said of the total, 450,000 tonnes is for delivery during the 1996/97 marketing year and 50,000 tonnes is for delivery in the 1997/98 marketing year.

WHEAT SALE - The Commodity Credit Corp of the U.S. Department of Agriculture said it had bought 35,540 tonnes of U.S. soft red winter wheat from Continental Grain for donation to Eritrea. The wheat was priced at $163.94 per tonne, FOB Westwego, and was for October 30-November 25 delivery.

CORN AND SOYBEAN SALES - Taiwan's Hui Shung group on Wednesday bought two combined shipments of U.S. soybeans and corn totalling 108,000 tonnes from Continental, traders said. Each shipment includes 38,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn.

CORN AND SOYBEAN SALES (cont.) - State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp on Wednesday bought a combined shipment of 18,000 tonnes of No.2 orbetter U.S. yellow corn and 12,000 tonnes of No.2 or better U.S.yellow soybeans from Mitsui. The combined shipment is slated for delivery from the U.S. Gulf of Mexico from November 1 to 15 with 12,000 tonnes soybeans at US$277.64/FOB and 18,000 tonnes at US$139.73/FOB.

SOYOIL SALE - The Dominican Republic bought 24,000 tonnes of South American soybean oil on Wednesday for February through May shipment. The purchase will be shipped in three 8,000-tonne loads, the first for February shipment at $530 a tonne, the second for April at $520 and the third for May at $505, all cost and freight. The Dominican Republic passed on a March shipment tender.
WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka is to seek October 17 100,000 tonnes optional-origin wheat for Nov 11-20 shipment.

WHEAT TENDERS (cont.) - Philippine flour mills rejected tenders for 53,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, traders said. "All the bids submitted were unrealistically high," an official from one of the buyers said. Philippine flour mills invited tenders earlier for 41,000 tonnes of dark northern spring wheat with a 14 percent protein content and 12,000 tonnes of western white wheat for November and December shipments.

WHEAT TENDERS - Morocco will tender on Thursday for 40,000 tonnes optional soft wheat for delivery in first half of November, the Office Interprofessionnel des Cereales et Legumineuses said. The tender's closing date is Thursday.

MARKET TALK - The world soymeal market is turning on China's axis as traders wait to see what move Chinese buyers will make next, Asian trading sources said. As the price of soymeal has fallen dramatically in the past week, talk has turned to Chinese buyers cancelling orders so they can buy back at cheaper prices. These rumors were superceded in late trading on Tuesday on CBOT by talk that China had re-entered the market after recent falls in futures prices.
... Soaring consumption for animal feeds will boost China's soymeal imports in 1996/97, USDA's Economic Research Service said Tuesday.
